title: Set 203

sentences.ko: 윗집 남자가 매일 밤 11시쯤만 되면 가구를 옮기는지 뭔지 하는데, 괜히 시끄럽다고 따지는 이웃은 되기 싫거든요. 근데 2주째 밤에 한 번도 안 깨고 자 본 적이 없어요.
sentences.text: The guy upstairs is moving furniture around or something every single night at like eleven, and I don't want to be that neighbor who complains, but I haven't slept through the night in two weeks.

alts.text: Upstairs guy's dragging furniture or whatever every night around eleven. I hate being that neighbor, but I haven't slept right in two weeks.

My upstairs neighbor appears to be moving furniture around every single night at approximately eleven o'clock. I would prefer not to be the sort of neighbor who complains, but I have not slept through the night in two weeks.

sentences.note: **slept through the night** 는 중간에 깨지 않고 아침까지 푹 잤다는 뜻입니다. **that neighbor who complains** 처럼 that 을 붙이면 다들 아는 그런 유형의 사람이라는 느낌이 납니다.

sentences.ko: 추수감사절에 삼촌 댁에 갔는데, 어떻게 알았는지 내가 회사 그만둔 걸 다들 벌써 알고 있더라. 그래서 저녁 내내 아니 나 방황하는 거 아니라고, 그냥 앞으로 뭐 할지 생각할 시간을 좀 갖는 거라고 설명했어.
sentences.text: We went to my uncle's for Thanksgiving, and somehow everybody already knew I'd quit my job, so I spent the whole dinner explaining that no, I'm not lost, I'm just taking some time to figure things out.

alts.text: So we did Thanksgiving at my uncle's, and somehow everyone already knew I quit my job. I spent the whole dinner going no, I'm not lost, I'm just taking some time to figure stuff out.

We spent Thanksgiving at my uncle's home, and somehow everyone was already aware that I had left my job, so I spent the entire dinner explaining that I am not lost; I am simply taking some time to work things out.

sentences.note: **figure things out** 는 앞으로 어떻게 할지 정리하고 답을 찾는다는 뜻입니다. **I'm not lost** 는 길을 잃은 게 아니라 인생에서 방황하는 게 아니라는 뜻으로 쓰였습니다.
sentences.situation: 친척들 모인 자리에서 질문 공세 받은 얘기

sentences.ko: 너희 아들 학교도 숙제를 전부 앱으로 보내? 나는 자꾸 놓쳐서, 금요일 밤에야 애가 그날 아침까지 내야 하는 과제가 있었다는 걸 알게 되거든.
sentences.text: Does your son's school do that thing where they send all the homework through an app? Because I keep missing stuff, and then I find out on Friday night that he had a project due that morning.

alts.text: Is your son's school doing the thing where all the homework goes through an app? I keep missing stuff, and then Friday night I find out he had a project due that morning.
Does your son's school send all of its homework assignments through an application? I ask because I keep missing things, and then I discover on Friday evening that he had a project due that morning.

sentences.note: **do that thing where** 는 다들 아는 어떤 방식을 꺼낼 때 쓰는 말로, 왜 그거 있잖아 ~하는 거 정도의 느낌입니다. **due** 는 그때까지 내야 한다는 뜻입니다.

sentences.ko: 메인 스트리트에 있는 그 피자집, 원래 내가 제일 좋아하던 데였는데 작년에 주인이 바뀌었어. 그 뒤로 값은 오르고 크기는 작아졌고, 솔직히 좀 냉동 피자 맛이 나.
sentences.text: That pizza place on Main used to be my favorite, but they got new owners last year, and now it costs more and it's smaller, and honestly it kind of tastes like frozen pizza.

alts.text: I used to love that pizza place on Main, but new owners took over last year, and now it's pricier and smaller and honestly it kinda tastes like frozen pizza.

The pizza restaurant on Main Street used to be my favorite, but it came under new ownership last year. It is now more expensive, the pizzas are smaller, and frankly, it tastes rather like frozen pizza.

sentences.note: **used to be my favorite** 는 예전에는 제일 좋아했지만 지금은 아니라는 뜻입니다. **kind of tastes like** 는 좀 ~ 같은 맛이 난다고 말을 부드럽게 할 때 씁니다.

sentences.ko: 솔직히 별거 없었어. 토요일에 파머스 마켓 가려고 했는데 딸이 아침에 일어나니까 열이 나서, 주말 내내 그냥 집에서 영화만 봤어. 지금은 괜찮아.
sentences.text: Not much, honestly. We were going to hit the farmers market on Saturday, but my daughter woke up with a fever, so we just stayed in and watched movies all weekend. She's fine now, though.

alts.text: Eh, not a lot. We were gonna do the farmers market Saturday, but my daughter woke up with a fever, so we just stayed home and watched movies all weekend. She's okay now though.

Not a great deal, to be honest. We had planned to visit the farmers market on Saturday, but my daughter woke up with a fever, so we stayed at home and watched films all weekend. She is well now, however.

sentences.note: **hit the farmers market** 의 hit 은 어디에 가다라는 뜻의 구어입니다. **stayed in** 은 밖에 안 나가고 집에 있었다는 뜻이고, 끝에 붙는 **though** 는 그래도라는 느낌을 줍니다.

reviewed: 1번 casual 이 text 의 뒷부분을 거의 그대로 되풀이해서 더 짧고 축약된 구어로 바꿨습니다 (I hate being that neighbor, haven't slept right).
3번 한국어의 '아이가' 는 친구끼리 하는 말로는 딱딱해서 '애가' 로 바꿨습니다.
3번 note 의 '그 왜 있잖아 ~하는 거 하는 느낌으로' 가 꼬여 있어서 알아듣기 쉽게 다시 썼습니다.
